newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Airport boost pushes Australian budget into black.
newsitem.headline: Airport boost pushes Australian budget into black.

text.p: The Australian government's finances have received an unbudgeted boost of almost A$2 billion from the sale of three major airports and are now comfortably in surplus for the fiscal year to June 1997.
The government, which announced the successful tenderers on Wednesday, confirms that the A$3.337 billion received for the airports is more than expected but refuses to say how much more.
"The prices we received are considerably higher than we anticipated might have been received before we started this process," Finance Minister John Fahey told reporters.
But the budget allowed just A$5.1 billion for asset sales.

Since this included A$3.4 billion from the sale of Commonwealth Bank and presumably something for Australian National, the federal government's railways, around A$1.5 billion is left for the airports.
That figure has now been exceeded by A$1.8 billion.
